description: Get statistics for a sequence. The steps array is the per-step breakdown: one entry per email step in graph order with its step number, automation nodeId, subject, and its own sent, delivered, bounced, opened, clicked, replies, and unsubscribed counts plus rates - so this is where you read how many of Email 4 went out, without reconstructing anything from list_sequence_events. Step counts come from the retained event stream, not the 14-day delivery history behind list_email_sends, so they stay answerable for old sends. Also returns the aggregate funnel across every step, attributed conversions and revenue (revenueCents), product recommendation funnel metrics, per-step failed subscribers and failure reasons, per-step Poll and NPS summaries in steps[].polls (lifetime, same shape as get_campaign_stats polls), and enrollmentSkipped counts for trigger matches where the contact could not be enrolled (unsubscribed/bounced). Pass period or start/end to use one explicit window for every historical metric; without them, step and aggregate counts are all-time and enrollmentSkipped defaults to the last 30 days. The enrollmentCounts field is a live snapshot of active and waiting enrollments grouped by current node, so it is not limited by period or start/end; contacts held by pause_sequence_subscribers are counted separately in pausedEnrollments. To compare the same step across many sequences in one call, use list_email_metrics instead.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

end.description: Optional ISO 8601 custom range end. Must be provided with start; maximum range is 90 days.

includeMachineEngagement.description: If true, include machine-classified bot/scanner opens and clicks. Defaults to false, so metrics and activity are human-only.

period.description: Optional sliding window: 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, or 90d. Ignored when start and end are provided.

start.description: Optional ISO 8601 custom range start. Must be provided with end.

name: get_sequence_stats

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `get_sequence_stats` MCP tool.

enrollmentCounts.description: Live enrollment-token counts for this sequence. Includes only active and waiting enrollments and is always a current snapshot, independent of historical period/start/end filters.

byCurrentNode.description: Live active and waiting enrollment counts grouped by the token's current sequence node.

items.description: Enrollment counts for one current sequence node.

active.description: Active enrollment count at this node.

currentNodeLabel.description: Current sequence node label or email subject when available.

currentNodeMissing.description: Whether the current node no longer exists in the sequence graph.

currentNodeType.description: Current sequence node type. Omitted when the node no longer exists in the graph.

total.description: Total active plus waiting enrollment count at this node.

waiting.description: Waiting enrollment count at this node.

total.description: Total active plus waiting enrollment count.

enrollmentSkipped.description: Trigger matches where an unsubscribed or bounced contact could not be enrolled, including the total count and counts grouped by reason. Uses the requested period or start/end range; without an explicit range, this field defaults to the last 30 days.

additionalProperties.description: Skipped enrollment count for this reason.

byReason.description: Skipped enrollment counts keyed by reason, such as unsubscribed or bounced.

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: Human-readable status, confirmation, or next-step message.

pausedEnrollments.description: Live count of enrollments held by pause_sequence_subscribers: total, and byCurrentNode (currentNodeId, currentNodeMissing, count). Kept separate from enrollmentCounts, whose active, waiting, and total exclude paused enrollments. Absent from API versions before per-subscriber pause.

recommendations.description: Product recommendation funnel aggregated across the sequence's email nodes: impressions, recipients, clicks, clickers, orders, legacy revenueCents, currency-safe revenueByCurrency totals, and topProducts. Present only when the sequence rendered product recommendation blocks.

sequence.description: The sequence record returned by Sequenzy. Run state: branch on effectiveStatus (draft, live, enrollment_paused, paused, or archived) rather than on status, which reads `active` even when new enrollments are paused. acceptsNewEnrollments and processesExistingEnrollments answer the two questions behind it, and effectiveStatusSummary is a plain-language sentence. The legacy triggerConfig.active flag is not read by the runtime; it is reported as a mirror of acceptsNewEnrollments. Email numbering: emails[].stepNumber and nodes[].config.stepNumber are legacy stored ordinals retained for compatibility. Prefer emails[].structuralStepNumber and nodes[].structuralStepNumber when explaining the visible sequence position. Structural numbers are graph-derived; emails in parallel branches intentionally share a depth. Sequences use sendingWindow for allowed local hours/days; they do not have Send Time Optimization. frequencyCapEnabled is true when email steps respect the company frequency cap (get_frequency_cap): contacts already at the cap skip the step. activeSubscribersOnly is true when only active contacts enter; when false, unsubscribed and bounced contacts still enter and only their marketing emails are skipped. STO is per-campaign (list_campaigns / get_campaign sendTimeOptimization).

stats.description: Delivery funnel across every email step in this sequence. `opened` and `clicked` are unique counts deduplicated by email send (one recipient opening five times counts once), not total open events. Every count is attributed to the sends made inside the requested window, including engagement that arrives after the window ends, so `opened <= delivered <= sent` always holds. Rates use `rateDenominator` (`delivered`, or `sent` when no delivery events were recorded, reported as `rateDenominatorBasis`); `deliveryRate` and `bounceRate` divide by `sent`.

steps.description: Per-step delivery funnel: one entry per email step of the sequence, in graph order, each with its own sent/delivered/opened/clicked counts. Read this to answer "how many of step N went out" - do not recount list_sequence_events. Counts come from the retained event stream, so they are not limited to the 14-day list_email_sends history. `opened` and `clicked` are unique counts deduplicated by email send (one recipient opening five times counts once), not total open events. Every count is attributed to the sends made inside the requested window, including engagement that arrives after the window ends, so `opened <= delivered <= sent` always holds. Rates use `rateDenominator` (`delivered`, or `sent` when no delivery events were recorded, reported as `rateDenominatorBasis`); `deliveryRate` and `bounceRate` divide by `sent`.

items.description: Metrics for one email step of the sequence.

failedCount.description: Contacts currently stuck on this step with a failed enrollment.

failedSubscribers.description: Up to 20 of the failed contacts on this step, as { subscriberId, email, failedAt, failedReason }.

items.description: One item in the returned collection.

nodeId.description: Automation node ID of this email step. Pass it to list_sequence_events or list_email_sends as automationNodeId to reach the individual recipients behind these counts, and it is the emailId that list_email_metrics reports for sequence emails.

polls.description: Poll and NPS summaries for this step, in the same shape as get_campaign_stats polls: each subscriber counts once per poll block with their latest answer. Lifetime results, not limited by period or start/end. Omitted when the step has no responses. Call list_poll_responses with this step's nodeId as campaignId to read the individual respondents.

items.description: One item in the returned collection.

stats.description: Delivery funnel for this step alone: sent, delivered, bounced, opened, clicked, replies, unsubscribed, and their rates. `opened` and `clicked` are unique counts deduplicated by email send (one recipient opening five times counts once), not total open events. Every count is attributed to the sends made inside the requested window, including engagement that arrives after the window ends, so `opened <= delivered <= sent` always holds. Rates use `rateDenominator` (`delivered`, or `sent` when no delivery events were recorded, reported as `rateDenominatorBasis`); `deliveryRate` and `bounceRate` divide by `sent`.

step.description: 1-based position of this email step in graph order. Step 4 is the fourth email a contact receives on the traversed path; on a branching graph, positions are assigned by traversal, so cross-check nodeId when a sequence forks.

subject.description: Subject line of the step's email, falling back to the node label, or null when neither is set.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
